solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scoundrel with gag

parts.note: to gag is to retch, heaving as if about to vomit

explanation.surface: A villain armed with a gag, perhaps for silencing a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a noun for a silencing cloth or a joke, but here it is the verb meaning to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is a contemptible, despicable person, so a synonym for a scoundrel.

clue.text: Rice dish recipe for starters — it's too complicated

indicators.note: for starters says only the first letter of the word recipe is used
complicated says the letters of the words before are tangled up

explanation.surface: A cook finds a rice dish recipe too complex to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: R, then 'complicated' rearranges ITSTOO into ISOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is the Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Speed discovered during post-mortem, possibly

indicators.note: discovered during says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pathologist finds evidence of drug use, speed, at an autopsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' suggests the drug that might turn up at an autopsy, but here it means rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the rate or pace of something, especially music, so speed.

clue.text: Shakespearean prince fleeing in the gloaming

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
flight is the act of fleeing

explanation.surface: Prince Hal running away at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the gloaming' is a Scots word for dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-light is the dim light of dusk or dawn, and the gloaming is twilight.

clue.text: Mother brought in slab on which a plate rests

indicators.note: brought in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a tablet is a flat slab, as of stone
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum carries in a slab of something for dinner, setting a plate on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on which a plate rests' reads as describing the slab, but it is the definition; 'brought in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A table mat is the protective pad placed under a plate or dish at table.

clue.text: Started to study at college around North

indicators.note: around says the pieces before it are placed on both sides of the following one

parts.note: to take a subject is to study it
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student began a course at university in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' at college is the British usage for being in residence at a university such as Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To have taken up a hobby or pursuit is to have started on it.

clue.text: Composer in seventh heaven

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ... was an English composer, Master of the Queen's Music
seventh heaven is a state of supreme happiness

explanation.surface: A musician in a state of ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss means perfect happiness, the same as being in seventh heaven, and Arthur Bliss was a composer.

clue.text: Power held by male here, surprisingly short-lived

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters land in an unexpected new order

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A man here holds power, but surprisingly briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' is only a link; 'surprisingly' rearranges P, MALE and HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time, transitory.

clue.text: Draw Turk's head in a pamphlet

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

indicators.note: head says the first letter of the word Turk's is taken

explanation.surface: A drawing of a Turk's head appears in a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside A TRACT, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, pull it in.

clue.text: Keith, appearing in 'Loot' with me, is cast in a film

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about or moulded anew, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor called Keith joins the speaker in a production of Joe Orton's play Loot, and is cast in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cast' reads as one phrase, but 'is' is part of the pool and 'cast' alone rearranges KEITH, LOOT, ME and IS. Loot is a farce by Joe Orton.
explanation.definitionFit: Some Like It Hot is the 1959 Billy Wilder comedy film starring Marilyn Monroe.

clue.text: Stumped by corset? There's a surprise!

parts.note: st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
a roll-on is an elasticated corset or girdle pulled on rather than laced

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer notes a batsman out stumped thanks to his corset: what a surprise!
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is 'stumped' when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while he is out of his ground. 'Stroll on!' is a British exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroll on is an informal British exclamation expressing surprise or disbelief, like 'well I never'.

clue.text: Article by a member on small boat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an MP is a Member of Parliament
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammar point about an article placed next to a member, on a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue convention for placing one piece after another; here it just joins, and the article lands last.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in East Asian rivers and harbours.

clue.text: Heated chow?

parts.note: heated means hot
a chow is a breed of dog, the chow chow

explanation.surface: Warmed-up food, chow being slang for grub.
explanation.walkthrough: Chow is slang for food, which is the whole-clue reading; the parts read chow as the Chinese dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A frankfurter sausage served warm in a bun is food, and chow is slang for food.

clue.text: Rail fare may be put away here

definitions.text: Rail fare may be put away here

parts.words: Rail fare may be put away here
parts.note: rail fare suggests the price of a train ticket, but means food on a train, and put away means eaten

explanation.surface: A place where a train ticket might be stowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' is food, not a ticket price, and 'put away' is to eat heartily.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage where meals are served lets passengers eat food on the train.

clue.text: Right of way coming from convent across it

indicators.note: the convent word spreads across, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: a priory is a religious house of monks or nuns, so a convent

explanation.surface: A road-user's precedence emerging from a nunnery's grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' is the container signal: the convent word spans around the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Priority on the road is the right to proceed ahead of other traffic, the right of way.

clue.text: Rain's rare for resort, but overdue

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort says the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Rain is unusual at a holiday resort, but long awaited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as re-sort, rearranging RAINS and RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment in arrears is behind schedule, so overdue.

clue.text: Title spelled backwards with wrong date, it's emerged

indicators.note: spelled backwards says the word for title is read from right to left

parts.note: a name is a title, as of a book

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of the next word are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A document comes out with its heading reversed and the wrong date on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelled backwards' turns NAME into EMAN; 'wrong' rearranges DATE into ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, so emanated is a synonym for emerged.

clue.text: Hurt, depressed English dramatist

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt
low means down, depressed

explanation.surface: An English playwright feeling wounded and miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurt, depressed English' reads as a description of the man, but splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was the Elizabethan playwright of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: First secretary perhaps losing little time finding official document

indicators.note: losing says a piece is dropped from the word before

parts.note: a first secretary is an embassy rank, so an example of a diplomat
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An embassy official, short of time, comes across a formal certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First secretary' is a diplomatic rank, hence 'perhaps' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is an official certificate, such as one conferring a qualification.

clue.text: A fund in hand for swimming maybe

parts.note: a float is a small sum of cash kept in hand, as in a till for giving change

explanation.surface: Money set aside for a swimming trip, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming maybe' is a definition by example: a swimmer is one way of being on the water's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Being afloat means buoyed up on water, which a swimmer is, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Style of interior design having red coat applied

indicators.note: applied, as paint is put on, says the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A decorating style featuring a coat of red paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied' signals rearranging REDCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s, used in interiors and architecture.

clue.text: Fruit — round variety

parts.note: O is round in shape
a range is a variety, as of goods

explanation.surface: A fruit described as round, available in several kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round variety' reads like a description of a fruit cultivar, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange is a common round citrus fruit.

clue.text: Horse-play?

parts.note: horseplay normally means rough fooling about, but split it is a stage play about horses

explanation.surface: Rough and boisterous fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Shaffer's play is named from the Latin word for horse and concerns a boy who blinds horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Equus is Peter Shaffer's 1973 play, its title the Latin for horse.

clue.text: Sponger ruined pair's tea

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the words that follow are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A freeloader spoils a couple's afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'pair's' counts as a letter here, joining PAIRS and TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite is someone who lives off others without giving back, a sponger or freeloader.

clue.text: Son's desire to be smart

parts.note: a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A boy wants to look well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' means stylish here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for fashionable and elegant, so smart.

clue.text: Continue a poem translated years ago

indicators.note: translated says the words are turned into another form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry on putting a poem into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges CONTINUE, A and POEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock opening of fairy tales means long ago, in years gone by.

clue.text: A banker's intoxicated state

indicators.note: intoxicated means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A financier is in a drunken condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a condition, as in a drunken state, but it is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the states of the USA, in the Great Plains.

clue.text: Student, at first, reportedly reserved in group

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of the word student is taken
reportedly says what follows is a word as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a reserved person is cool, distant in manner

explanation.surface: A shy student is said to have been held back from a class.
explanation.walkthrough: S, then CHOOL, said like 'cool'. 'Student' and 'reserved' suggest the classroom sense, but the definition is a group, as of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a large group of fish or whales swimming together.
